topic: Min-cost OD matrix from end supply/demand with shadow prices
idea: Balanced transportation LP: minimise sum c_ij x_ij with row sums = supplies and column sums = demands; dual variables u_i, v_j give the shadow price matrix s_ij = u_i + v_j - c_ij. A negative element signals a more-for-less solution: raising supply at source p and demand at destination q by delta lowers total cost (Szwarc condition; Mehar method steps 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.8).
does: Treat boundary ends' supply and demand (veh/h) as a transportation problem with cost = free-flow or measured travel time, solve for the minimum-cost OD matrix (transportation simplex/MODI, a few hundred stdlib lines) as an alternative to the gravity model, and report shadow prices: the marginal travel-time value of one more veh/h at an end, and pairs where more demand would cost less in the model.
inputs: end supplies and demands, OD travel-time matrix (from route search or one run)
outputs: minimum-cost OD matrix, dual values per end, list of negative shadow prices
existing: partial: gravity-model OD generation; no cost-optimal assignment or marginal values
notes: A cost-minimising OD is not how drivers behave (user-equilibrium vs system optimum), so label it a system-optimum bound; the book is pure OR with no traffic content.

topic: Triangular fuzzy demand as a three-scenario sensitivity
idea: Symmetric triangular fuzzy numbers (a - spread, a, a + spread) for supply, demand and cost, ordered by ranking functions, reduce to crisp LPs on the mode and bounds.
does: Let the assistant state uncertain end flows as a mode and spread and automatically run low, mode and high demand scenarios through run_experiment, reporting KPI ranges.
inputs: flow mode and spread per end
notes: Plain 3-point sensitivity; no fuzzy arithmetic needed.
